p: Version: 1.2
Figma design: https://www.figma.com/design/DR4gEODShYgJqkozs3mF5q/Working---ShopView-App?node-id=11817-27678&t=jkmK950Ycg9iWHfT-1
Claude design: https://claude.ai/design/p/fac6efcf-a972-4c02-96a5-def12ed8b037?file=Filters.html&via=share
Parts filters design: https://www.figma.com/design/DR4gEODShYgJqkozs3mF5q/Working---ShopView-App?node-id=11884-16885
Reports filters design: https://www.figma.com/design/DR4gEODShYgJqkozs3mF5q/Working---ShopView-App?node-id=11903-10573
Page search component: https://www.figma.com/design/DR4gEODShYgJqkozs3mF5q/Working---ShopView-App?node-id=11829-8908

Users managing large volumes of work orders need to quickly narrow down the list to a relevant subset: by status, customer, technician, advisor, or on-site asset status. Currently, the Work Orders page lacks a dedicated filter bar, forcing users to scroll through long lists or rely on the tab shortcuts (Estimates, Completed) as the only filtering mechanism. This makes day-to-day triage slower and increases the chance of missing urgent work orders. Adding a persistent, multi-criteria filter bar directly addresses this pain point and aligns ShopView with the workflow expectations of shop managers and service advisors.

li.p: A filter bar appears below the tab navigation on the Work Orders page, providing quick access to five filters: Status, Customer, Lead Technician, Service Advisor, and Asset on Site
Each filter is a labelled chip that opens a dropdown panel when clicked
Status, Customer, Lead Technician, and Service Advisor are multi-select filters; Asset on Site is a two-option (Yes / No) dropdown
Customer, Lead Technician, and Service Advisor dropdowns include a search field to quickly locate a specific value
When one or more values are selected in a filter, the chip updates to display the selected values and a "Clear filters" button appears in the filter bar
The filter bar can be collapsed and expanded via a toggle in the page toolbar; when collapsed with active filters, the toolbar toggle shows a visual indicator
Filter selections persist when the user navigates away from the Work Orders page and returns
The active filter state is reflected in the page URL, enabling users to share or bookmark a filtered view
Filters apply to all tabs except where noted (see Tab Behavior, Story 9)
Supported on both desktop and mobile

A filter bar appears below the page header on each view of the Parts area (Inventory, Part Sales, Catalog, Returns, Credits, Purchase Orders, Vendor Invoices, Vendors), following the same chip-and-dropdown pattern as Work Orders

Filters are context-specific per view: each view shows only the chips relevant to its data (e.g., Inventory filters by Bin Location, Category, Supply, and Vendor; Purchase Orders by Vendor, Status, Date, and Ordered by)

Entity filters (Customer, Vendor, Created by, Ordered by, Received by, Processed by) use the searchable multi-select dropdown; long lists such as Category and Manufacturer also include a search field; short attribute filters (Supply, Part Type, Bin Location, State/Province, Status) use the checkbox list
Date-based columns (Date, Invoice date, Date received) use the new date-range filter
Active-chip appearance, "Clear filters", "Clear selection", collapse/expand, per-view persistence, URL state, and mobile behavior all match the Work Orders definitions
A filter bar appears below the report header on each report, following the same chip-and-dropdown pattern as Work Orders

Filters are context-specific per report: nearly every report includes a Date filter as its primary scoping control, alongside the entity dimensions relevant to that report (Customer, Vendor, Technician, Advisor, Staff, Employee, and so on)

A new date-range filter type is introduced: the chip opens a start/end date picker with no presets and no default range selected — the user always chooses the period, and the range applies immediately when the second date is picked. The selected range is reflected in the URL (e.g., range=custom&from=2026-04-01&to=2026-04-25) so a filtered report is shareable
Reports with sub-report tabs keep a separate filter set per tab
Active-chip appearance, "Clear filters", "Clear selection", collapse/expand, persistence, URL state, and mobile behavior all match the Work Orders definitions
Each list page gains a search control in the page toolbar, sitting alongside the filter bar toggle and the primary action. It narrows the records on that page only
The control is collapsed by default (magnifier icon + "Search") and expands in place into a text input when clicked, on both desktop and mobile
Search applies as the user types — no apply button — and works additively with the filter bar: a query narrows within the active filters, and vice versa
Available on every list page across Work Orders, Parts and Reports, on desktop and mobile
Because page-level narrowing now lives on the page, the global header search stops filtering page content — this behaviour is removed app-wide (Story 14)

p: When I'm opening my work queue at the start of the day, I want to filter work orders by technician and status, so I can see exactly what's in progress for my team without scrolling through everything.
When a customer calls about their vehicle, I want to filter by customer name, so I can instantly see all their open work orders.
When I'm doing a lot check, I want to filter by "Asset on Site: Yes", so I can see only vehicles currently on premises.
When I'm counting stock, I want to filter Inventory by Bin Location and Category, so I can verify quantities for one shelf without scrolling the whole catalog.
When a vendor invoice arrives, I want to filter Vendor Invoices by Vendor and Date received, so I can find and reconcile the matching record quickly.
When I run month-end A/R aging, I want to set the Date range and filter by Customer, so I can produce the exact statement a customer is disputing.
When I review payroll, I want to filter Timesheets by Employee and a pay-period Date range, so I can approve hours for one person at a time.
When I know the work order number but not who it belongs to, I want to type it straight into the page, so I can jump to it without setting up a filter.
When I have already filtered Inventory down to one bin, I want to search within that result, so I can find one part without clearing my filters.

li.p: Reduce time to find a relevant subset of work orders
Allow multi-criteria filtering in a single interaction
Persist filter state to avoid re-applying filters on every visit
Enable sharing of filtered views via URL
Asset on Site changed from toggle to dropdown to maintain visual and interaction consistency with the other four filters, all of which use the dropdown chip pattern.
No selection limit on multi-select filters — users can select as many values as needed.
"Clear filters" clears all active filters at once; a separate "Clear selection" action within each dropdown clears only that filter individually.

Status filter is hidden on the Estimates and Completed tabs — those tabs are shortcuts that already pre-filter by a single status, so showing a Status filter would be redundant and potentially confusing.
My Work Orders tab does not remove filters: filters continue to work on top of the user-scoped result set.
Filters persist in session and across navigation: the filter state is saved per user and reloaded when they return to the Work Orders page.

Context-specific filter sets on Parts and Reports: each Parts view and each Report defines its own filter chips rather than sharing a single set, because the underlying datasets and relevant dimensions differ per view.

New date-range filter type: Date chips open a custom start/end picker — no presets, no default range — and apply immediately on selection of the second date. Used across Reports and the date columns on Parts views.

Parts and Reports selections are scoped to their view/tab and persist there: filters do not carry across Parts views, Report tabs, or sub-report tabs; each view/tab retains its own selections and restores them on return.
Long enumerations get a search field: Category and Manufacturer use the searchable dropdown rather than a plain checkbox list.
Multi-select where it makes sense: all Parts and Reports filters are multi-select except the date-range filter, which is a single range.

Page search is separate from the filter bar, not a filter chip. It lives in the toolbar row with the collapse toggle and primary action; the chips stay in the row below. The two are additive but independently cleared — "Clear filters" does not clear the query, and clearing the query does not clear the chips.

Global search no longer filters page content. Narrowing the current list is now the job of the page's own filters and search. The global search filtering behaviour is removed across the whole application, not only on the pages covered by these designs.

One shared search component across all pages, scoped strictly to its own page. Page-specific behaviour is configuration (which fields are searched), not a per-module variant. Each page's search input queries only the records in that page's table — it cannot reach content on any other page, in any other module, or anywhere outside that table. Cross-page and cross-module lookup is the job of the global header search, which is the whole basis for the split in Story 14.

Generic placeholder. The expanded field reads "Type to search" on every page rather than being parameterised per page, unlike the filter dropdowns which use targeted copy ("Search customer", "Search technician").

Mobile and desktop use one pattern, not two. Search expands inline in the action row on both, with the same four component states. Two layout changes make this possible on a 370px mobile row: the primary CTA stops stretching and uses its natural hug width (144px for "New Work Order", the same as desktop) instead of filling the row at 211px; and pages with more than one icon-only action collapse those into a "more" kebab. Together these free enough space for the field to expand with every other control still visible. No modal, no separate search screen, no active-query indicator, and no mobile-only variant to maintain.
Hover-on-expanded, disabled and loading states are out of scope for this release; the component does not define them.

S8-R4: The empty state includes a prompt or link to clear filters and, where a search query is active, to clear the query

h3: Story 9: Tab Behaviour with Active Filters
p: As a user, I want filters to work correctly as I switch between Work Orders tabs so that my filtered view is consistent.
Design: https://www.figma.com/design/DR4gEODShYgJqkozs3mF5q/Working---ShopView-App?node-id=11854-23562 Jira: TBD

li.p: The user is on the Work Orders page
S9-R1: On the All tab, all five filters (Status, Customer, Lead Technician, Service Advisor, Asset on Site) are shown and active
S9-R2: On the Estimates tab, the Status filter chip is hidden; the remaining four filters are shown and apply on top of the Estimates pre-filter
S9-R3: On the Completed tab, the Status filter chip is hidden; the remaining four filters are shown and apply on top of the Completed pre-filter
S9-R4: On the My Work Orders tab, all five filters are shown; the table already scopes results to work orders assigned to the logged-in user, and the filters apply on top of that scope

S9-R5: Filter selections are maintained when switching between tabs; selections that are incompatible with a tab (e.g., a Status selection on the Estimates tab) are not applied but are retained in memory so they reappear if the user switches back to the All tab
S9-N1: A Status selection made on the All tab does not carry over visually to the Estimates or Completed tabs, but is not lost

p: As a user, I want my filter selections to be remembered so that I don't have to re-apply them every time I visit the Work Orders page.
Jira: TBD

li.p: The user has previously applied one or more filters on the Work Orders page
S10-R1: When the user navigates away from the Work Orders page (e.g., to a Work Order detail, then back), the filter selections and collapsed/expanded state are restored exactly as they were left

p.ac:inline-comment-marker: S10-R2: Filter selections persist for the duration of the browser session
S10-R3: Filter selections are saved per user: one user's filters do not affect another user's view

li.p: S10-R4: The active search query persists on the same terms as filter selections — restored when the user navigates away and returns (S10-R1), retained for the duration of the browser session (S10-R2), and saved per user (S10-R3)
S10-R5: Filters and the search query are restored together and reapply additively (S13-R10), so the user returns to exactly the result set they left
S10-N1: If a previously selected filter value no longer exists (e.g., a customer was deleted), the system silently ignores that value and the filter updates to reflect only valid selections
S10-N2: If a restored query no longer matches any records because the underlying data has changed, the table shows the empty state (Story 8). The query is not silently discarded

p: As a user, I want the active filter state to be reflected in the page URL so that I can share or bookmark a filtered view.
Jira: TBD

li.p: The user is on the Work Orders page
S11-R1: When a user applies one or more filters, the page URL updates to reflect the active filter state

p.ac:inline-comment-marker: S11-R2: When a user opens a URL that contains filter state, the Work Orders page loads with those filters pre-applied and the table already filtered

li.p: S11-R3: If the URL contains a filter value that no longer exists (e.g., a deleted customer), the system ignores that value and loads the page without it
S11-R4: The active search query is reflected in the page URL alongside the filter state, so a filtered-and-searched view can be shared or bookmarked
S11-R5: Opening a URL that contains a search query loads the page with that query pre-applied and the search control in its filled state, matching the filter behaviour in S11-R2
S11-N1: If the URL filter state is malformed or unrecognizable, the page loads without any filters applied and does not show an error
S11-N2: If the URL search parameter is malformed, the page loads without a query applied and does not show an error, matching S11-N1

p: As a mobile user, I want to access filters on the Work Orders page so that I can narrow down results on a smaller screen.
Design: https://www.figma.com/design/DR4gEODShYgJqkozs3mF5q/Working---ShopView-App?node-id=11857-31046 Jira: TBD

li.p: The user is accessing Work Orders on a mobile device
S12-R1: The filter chips are displayed in a horizontally scrollable row below the tab navigation
S12-R2: The filter chips behave identically to desktop: tapping a chip opens its dropdown, selections update the chip appearance, "Clear filters" appears when active
S12-R3: Filter dropdowns open as a bottom sheet or overlay appropriate for the mobile viewport
S12-R4: The filter bar collapse toggle is not shown on mobile — the filter bar is always visible

S12-R5: The page search control is shown on mobile and behaves as it does on desktop (Story 13, S13-R16 to S13-R21). S12-R4, which hides the filter bar collapse toggle on mobile, does not apply to the search control
S12-N1: If no work orders match the active filters on mobile, the list shows the same empty state as desktop

p: As a user, I want to search within the page I'm on so that I can find a specific record without setting up a filter.
Design: https://www.figma.com/design/DR4gEODShYgJqkozs3mF5q/Working---ShopView-App?node-id=11829-8908 Jira: TBD

li.p: The user is on a list page that supports page search (see S13-R22)
S13-R1: A Search control is displayed in the page toolbar, in the right-hand action group, positioned before any icon-only actions and before the primary CTA

S13-R2: In its default state the control is a low-emphasis text button: magnifier icon (20×20) and the label "Search", Inter Medium 14/20, grey/600 (#4B5565), 8px corner radius, transparent background, 10px padding
S13-R3: On hover the control takes a grey/100 (#EEF2F6) background fill; the label colour is unchanged

S13-R4: On desktop, clicking the control expands it in place into a text input and moves focus into the input. The field grows leftward from its anchor and the remaining toolbar actions stay in position. The expanded width is 180px
S13-R5: The expanded empty state shows the magnifier icon, the text caret, and the placeholder "Type to search" in grey/500 (#697586)
S13-R6: Once the user types, the entered text is shown in grey/900 (#121926) and an X-circle clear icon (16×16) appears at the right edge of the field
S13-R7: The query applies as the user types, debounced. There is no apply or submit button and Enter is not required. Debounce interval is not specified in the design — 300ms proposed

S13-R8: Long queries use standard text input behaviour: the field neither grows nor truncates, the text scrolls horizontally within it, and the caret follows the insertion point. Keyboard navigation and click-and-drag selection behave as in any text input

S13-R9: Search is scoped strictly to the records in the current page's table. It never returns results from another page, another module, or any content outside that table — no cross-page lookup, no fallback to a wider search when the query returns nothing
S13-R10: Search and filters are additive (AND). A query narrows within the active filters; applying a filter narrows within the active query
S13-R11: On pages with tabs, search applies within the active tab only
S13-R12: Results replace the table contents in place. There is no separate results view or results page

S13-R13: Clicking the X-circle clears the query and restores the list to its filtered-but-unsearched state. "Clear filters" (S8-R1) does not clear the search query, and clearing the search query does not clear any filters

S13-R14: The search query is retained while the user remains on the page, including across tab switches, sorting and pagination. Retention beyond the page — across navigation and for the session — is covered by S10-R4, and URL state by S11-R4
S13-R15: On desktop, blur with an empty field collapses the control to its default state. Blur with a query keeps the field expanded so the active query stays visible

S13-R16: Mobile uses the same inline expansion as desktop. There is no modal, no separate search screen, and no mobile-only state in the component. Tapping the collapsed control expands it in place within the action row, moves focus into the field and raises the keyboard

S13-R17: On mobile the expanded field fills the remaining width of the action row rather than taking the fixed 180px desktop width. On Work Orders that resolves to 162px. All other toolbar actions remain visible and in position throughout — nothing is hidden while searching

S13-R18: To create that room, the primary CTA on mobile uses its natural hug width instead of stretching to fill the row — "New Work Order" is 144px, the same width it has on desktop, not 211px. The action group is right-aligned as on desktop, so the free space sits to the left and the field expands into it

S13-R19: Where a page has more than one icon-only action in its toolbar, those actions collapse into a single "more" kebab on mobile. This applies to Inventory, Purchase Orders, Timesheet Activities, both Technician Efficiency reports, Sales Tax (Collected), and any other page carrying two or more icon actions

S13-R20: No separate active-query indicator is needed on mobile. Because the field stays expanded and visible whenever a query is present, the desktop blur rules (S13-R15) apply unchanged: empty collapses, non-empty stays expanded showing the query

S13-R21: All query behaviour is identical across breakpoints — additive with filters (S13-R10), tab scoping (S13-R11), clearing (S13-R13), retention (S13-R14) and the four component states (S13-R2 to S13-R6). Only the expanded width differs, and that is a fill rule rather than a distinct behaviour

S13-R22: The control is present on every list page in Work Orders (Work Orders, Estimates), Parts (Inventory, Part Sales, Catalog, Returns, Credits, Purchase Orders, Vendor Invoices, Vendors) and Reports (Timesheet Activities, Timesheets, Sales, Technician Efficiency (Invoiced), Technician Efficiency (Completed), Advisor Analysis, Shop Efficiency, Work In Progress, Sales Follow Up, Sales Tax (Collected), Sales Tax (All Tax Rates), A/R Aging Summary, A/R Aging Detail, A/R Aging Collection, A/P Aging Summary, A/P Aging Detail, A/P Unpaid Invoices, IBS Batch Transactions, Quickbooks Unexported Items, Notes, Reminders)

S13-R23: Each page defines its own set of searchable fields. Default: the human-readable identifier columns visible in the table (record number, customer name, asset, part number, part description, vendor name, invoice number). Numeric, currency and date columns are excluded — those are served by filters
S13-N1: If no records match the query, the table shows an empty state (see Story 8)
S13-N2: If the query is cleared while filters remain active, the table returns to the filtered result set rather than the unfiltered list
S13-N3: Hover states for the expanded field, and disabled and loading states, are not defined and are out of scope for this release
S13-E1: If the user collapses the filter bar (S1-R5) while a search query is active, the query continues to apply and the search control remains in the toolbar

h3: Story 14: Global Search — Remove Page Filtering
p: As a user, I want the global header search to take me to records rather than silently filter the page I'm on, so that narrowing a list is done by that page's own filters and search.
Jira: TBD

li.p: Page search (Story 13) is available on the page in question
S14-R1: The global header search returns navigational results only. It takes the user to a record or page and does not modify the contents of the list the user is currently viewing
S14-R2: The existing code path that applies a global search query as a filter on the current page's table is removed, not hidden behind a flag or left dormant
S14-R3: Any state, URL parameters or persisted values that carry a global search term into page-level filtering are removed with it
S14-R4: Entering a query in the global search while on a list page leaves that list untouched

S14-R5: This applies to every page in the application, not only the pages listed in S13-R22. Global search must no longer alter the visible record set anywhere — including pages outside Work Orders, Parts and Reports, pages with no design in the current explorations, and pages that do not receive a page search control. QA should treat this as an app-wide sweep, not a per-module check

S14-R6: Any page affected by S14-R5 that is not covered by S13-R22 will lose text-based narrowing entirely. Each such page must be identified and an explicit decision recorded: give it a page search control, or accept the loss

S14-N1: Page search (Story 13) is a hard prerequisite. Removing global-search filtering from a page before page search is available there would leave that page with no way to narrow by text. If the rollout is phased, S14-R2 is scoped per page and S14-R5 is verified once at the end

p: Note on persistence and URL state. S10 persists state per user and S11 restores it from the URL. The two can disagree — a user with a persisted query who opens a shared link carrying a different one. The existing behaviour has the same tension for filters, so this is not new, but it becomes more likely once two things are being restored. Worth a precedence rule (URL wins on load, then persists) in whichever story owns it.
